featured_reviews.name: Prashant K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sai Dham Mandir, located near Thakur Complex along the Western Express Highway (WEH), is a well-known spiritual destination for devotees. However, several concerns need attention for an improved experience.

Concerns & Challenges:
1.	Noise, Dust & Pollution:
•	The temple’s proximity to WEH leads to constant traffic noise and air pollution.
•	It lacks the peace and serenity that devotees seek in a spiritual place.
2.	Vendors & Commercialization:
•	Numerous vendors outside the temple aggressively sell Pooja-related goods, making the entrance feel more like a business hub than a temple.
3.	Oil Spill & Safety Hazards:
•	The Shani Dev section has significant oil spillage due to devotees offering mustard oil.
•	Despite regular cleaning by temple administration, the slippery floors pose a high risk of falls, especially for elderly devotees and children.
4.	Presence of Beggars & Lack of Facilities for Them:
•	Many poor people beg outside the temple, constantly approaching visitors.
•	They lack proper shelter, often standing or sitting under the flyover shade.

Recommendations for Improvement:
•	Temple trustees should allocate additional funds for:
•	Enhanced cleanliness & safety measures (especially in the Shani Dev section).
•	Providing sheds, drinking water, and basic food facilities for the underprivileged outside the temple.
•	Better management of vendors to maintain the temple’s sanctity.

Final Thoughts:

While Sai Dham Mandir remains a holy place for spiritual seekers, the overall experience is hindered by external disturbances and safety issues. With better maintenance, crowd control, and enhanced support for the underprivileged, it can truly become a tranquil and divine space for devotees.

featured_reviews.name: Rajiv Lavangare
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Sai Dham Temple located near Thakur complex adjoining the highway is a beautiful and peaceful place of worship that I recently visited. The temple is dedicated to Sai Baba, but also has many other Hindu gods for worship. The atmosphere is serene and calm, making it the perfect place for meditation and reflection.

The temple is well-maintained and immaculately clean. The walls are adorned with beautiful paintings and sculptures of many  Hindu deities, and the aroma of incense fills the air. The priests are friendly and welcoming, and they perform the rituals and prayers with great devotion and sincerity.

The Sai Dham Temple is open to people of all faiths, and everyone is welcome to come and worship. The temple offers a sense of peace and tranquility that is hard to find in our busy lives. I left the temple feeling spiritually rejuvenated and inspired.

Overall, I highly recommend the Sai Dham Temple to anyone who is seeking a quiet and peaceful place of worship. The temple is a true gem and a must-visit for anyone interested in Hindu spirituality.

Parking: The service road has lots of space to park your cars & bikes.

featured_reviews.name: Dr Rajan D Walawalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Shree Krusangalidevi temple is situated at Akurli Village Kandivli East .This temple was built approximately in year 1845.Initially it was a small wooden temple .The present temple  is a renovated structure .Around the premises of the temple there are temples of Shree Siddheshwar Mahadev,Shree Sitaladevi,Shree Datta,Dakshinmukhi Shree Hanuman.The idol of Shree Krusanglidevi was found at the base of a pond in the area approximately in 1845 and it was installed and temple built .Some also refer the Goddess as Shree Akurli Devi.The Akurli road is named after Shree Akurlidevi.On Magh poornima ie.  Full moon day in the month of Magh as per Hindu calander year celebration on a large scale is held in the temple premises on the occasion of Vardhapan din ie. the day on which Shree Krusangli Akurli Mata idol was installed in the temple. In the month of Ashwin celebrations on large scale are held during Navratri days and culminating on Dassera.In front of Shree Krusangli Akurli Mata Mandir on the eastern side a tall lamp-post is installed ,in marathi it is called Deepastambh  and a flag pole called as dhwajastambh in marathi.This temple is within 8 minutes walking distance from Kandivli station on the east side .Following auspicious days are celebrated in the premises of the temple in a year ,Maghi poornima(Shree Krusangli Goddess Utsav)in Magh,Mahashivratri in Magh,Holi in Phalgun,Gudipadhwa in Chaitra,Shree Ramnavmi in Chaitra,Shree Hanuman Jayanti in Chaitra,Watapoornima in Jyeshta,Shravani Somwar in Shravan,Shree Krishna Jayanti(Janmashtami)in Shravan,Haritalika in Bhadrapad,Navratri Utsav arambh in Ashwin,Lalita Panchami in ashwin,Maha Ashtami Homahavan in ashwin,Vijayadashmi(Dassera) in ashwin,Tulsi Viwaha in Kartik and Datta jayanti in Margashirsh month as per hindu calander.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Jogeshwari Mandir, Mumbai | A Powerful Spiritual Experience with Mahadev’s Energetic Shiv Ling

Jogeshwari Mandir in Mumbai is one of those rare temples where the spiritual energy is felt instantly—quietly, deeply, and unmistakably. As a staunch Hindu believer, my visit here was not just a darshan, but a genuinely soul-stirring experience that stayed with me long after I stepped out.

🛕 First Impressions & Temple Vibration

The moment you approach the temple, there is a strong sense of sanctity and tradition. Despite being located in bustling Mumbai, the inner space feels like a spiritual cocoon—calm, devotional, and grounded. The atmosphere naturally encourages silence, prayer, and gratitude.

🔱 Special Mention: The Powerful Shiv Ling of Mahadev

The highlight of this temple for me was the Shiv Ling of Mahadev—truly powerful and radiating with an intense, divine energy. Standing in front of the Shiv Ling, you feel a deep stillness, as if the space itself is charged with devotion and centuries of faith.

For devotees of Lord Shiva, this is not a casual stop—it feels like an experience of presence. The darshan brings a sense of strength and peace simultaneously, and the energy around the sanctum is something I would describe as palpably spiritual.

🌺 Darshan Experience & Devotee Flow

Even during peak times, darshan is managed with respect and discipline. The temple maintains an orderly flow, allowing devotees enough time to connect, pray, and absorb the spiritual atmosphere without feeling rushed. The collective chants, the bells, and the devotion in the air elevate the experience further.

🧼 Cleanliness, Maintenance & Overall Comfort

The premises are well-maintained and clean, reflecting reverence for the deity and consideration for devotees. For seniors and families, the environment feels safe and manageable—an important point for those planning a spiritual visit in Mumbai.

📍 Location & Accessibility

Located in Jogeshwari, the temple is accessible for residents and visitors from Andheri, Goregaon, Malad, and other nearby areas. If you’re searching for:
•	Jogeshwari Mandir Mumbai
•	Shiv Mandir in Jogeshwari
•	Mahadev Shiv Ling darshan Mumbai
•	spiritual places in Mumbai
this temple should definitely be on your list.

🕉️ Why This Temple Stands Out

✅ Deep spiritual vibration even in a busy city
✅ Mahadev’s Shiv Ling radiating powerful energy
✅ Traditional sanctity and peaceful ambience
✅ Disciplined darshan management
✅ A true place for prayer, reflection, and inner grounding

⭐ Final Verdict

⭐ 5/5 — for the divine atmosphere, powerful darshan, and the extraordinary spiritual presence of Mahadev.

Jogeshwari Mandir is a reminder that faith is alive and deeply rooted in Mumbai. If you seek a temple where you can truly feel Mahadev’s presence, this is a must-visit.

🙏 Har Har Mahadev 🙏

featured_reviews.name: vishal sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
It is ancient rock cut cave temple nestled amidst the bustling narrow lanes of Jogeshwari area. The construction time of the cave temple is said to be mid first century. The carvings are not much intricate but there are imposing columnades and verandahs. The rock has been cut vertically downward as in Ellora. It represents massive human work of those days

There us Jagdamba temple in central and also Ganesh and Dattatreya temple in other niches. Ma Shakti is enshrined in foot carvings form. Ganesh is massive and vermillion coated. Dattatreya is small and etched on vertical rock surface.

Caves are under ASI protection but not maintained well and is encroached upon. It is the locality people who are doing the needful.

Jogeshwari or Yogeshwari is a Sanskrit name which means "Goddess Durga".
The temple contain impressions of Goddess Jogeshwari’s footprints.
You can buy flowers, coconut and other offerings from the shop outside the cave.
Regular pujas  and havans are performed to the Devi here.
The cave temple is so ancient that the near by area itself is known by the name Jogeshwari.
It is very imperturbable place.
Parking area is not available.
